content.text: Precondition allows k = s.Length + 1; should be k <= s.Length.

input.command:
cat > diagnosis.json <<'EOF'
{"spec_element": "requires",
 "proof_obligation": "initiation",
 "diagnosis": "The precondition of ReverseUptoK allows k == s.Length + 1, so l = k - 1 == s.Length and indices s[l-i], s[k-1-i] etc. (with i = 0) are out of bounds in the postcondition, invariants and loop body. The precondition should be 2 <= k <= s.Length."}
EOF
sed -i 's/requires 2 <= k <= (s.Length) + 1/requires 2 <= k <= s.Length/' program.dfy && dafny verify program.dfy

content.text:
Fixed: Dafny now verifies `program.dfy` with 4 verified and 0 errors. The command still exits with code 2. That's only because of style warnings about unneeded semicolons in the original code; it has nothing to do with verification.

**What was wrong:** The precondition of `ReverseUptoK` (line 19) allowed `k` to be `s.Length + 1`. In that case `l = k - 1` equals `s.Length`. So with `i = 0`, `s[l-i]` reads one past the end of the array, and so does `s[k-1-i]` in the postcondition. That out-of-bounds index triggered every error, in the postcondition (line 20), the loop invariants (lines 27–28) and the swap in the loop body (line 31). The counterexamples all show exactly this, with `k = s.Length + 1`.

**Fix:** I changed the precondition to `requires 2 <= k <= s.Length`.

`diagnosis.json` records this as a `requires` / `initiation` problem.
